Unscrupulous

un-SKROO-pyuh-lus -- stress on the second syllable, SKROO. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Unscrupulous is having no moral principles.

The unscrupulous manager pocketed the waitstaff's tips and dared anyone to complain.

Worked Example

A talent scout signs young athletes to contracts he knows are unfair, betting that their families will never read the fine print.

The scout is unscrupulous: nothing inside him objects to cheating people who trust him. An unscrupulous person is not just dishonest once -- they are missing the moral brakes entirely.

How Unscrupulous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

unprincipled

unprincipled: lacking moral standards

dishonest

dishonest: not truthful or fair

corrupt

corrupt: willing to act dishonestly for personal gain

Antonyms

ethical

ethical: guided by moral principles

scrupulous

scrupulous: extremely careful to do what is right

How Strong Is It? — dishonest → unscrupulous → corrupt

dishonest vs. unscrupulous

dishonest vs. unscrupulous: Dishonest is the lighter charge -- a dishonest answer bends the truth once, while an unscrupulous person has no moral principles at all, ready to cheat whenever cheating pays.

corrupt vs. unscrupulous

corrupt vs. unscrupulous: Corrupt goes even beyond unscrupulous: an unscrupulous dealer will cheat when the chance appears, while a corrupt official has turned dishonesty into a system, selling out the very duty they were trusted with.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of unscrupulous.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — un-

prefix — un-: not (Old English un-)

root — scrupul-

root — scrupul-: a small sharp stone; a nagging doubt of conscience (Latin scrupulus, diminutive of scrupus 'rough pebble')

suffix — -ous

suffix — -ous: full of; possessing the qualities of (Latin -osus, via Old French -ous)

Put it together

Put it together: Unscrupulous uses the -ous variant of this unit's suffix family, with un- ('not') reversing the whole package. Latin scrupulus was a small sharp stone -- the pebble in your shoe -- which the Romans made a metaphor for the nagging prick of conscience. A scrupulous person is 'full of' those little stones of doubt about doing wrong; an UNscrupulous person walks in perfect comfort, because no pebble of conscience ever bothers them at all.

Use the root in a new word: scruple

Use the root in a new word: scruple: Her scruples would not let her copy even a single answer, no matter how stuck she was.

Root Check

Word Choice

Unscrupulous is stronger than dishonest: it describes a settled character, not a single lapse. It gravitates toward people who exploit trust for gain -- unscrupulous dealers, landlords, promoters, lenders. Its positive twin scrupulous is worth learning alongside it: same pebble of conscience, kept versus discarded.
